rv.q: An exceptionally good show is now on stage at Chicago’s Trap Door Theatre. This wonder— The Man Who Fell with the Rain — has been translated through three languages on its way to the footlights in its U.S. premiere, right here on the tiny stage on Cortland Ave.
It's a tad long and runs thin on momentum toward the end. But it is well-acted and staged, with the clarity and humor of a good folk tale.
It's amusing and delightfully weird because it's being staged by Trap Door Theatre, directed by Kay Martinovich.
The Man Who Fell with the Rain isn't a bad play, but it isn't a good one either.
This version, however, is not as good. Kureichick's script is not without its charms, nor without its humor, but ultimately this story may not support a full stage version.

Despite finding my own interest fading along with the town's, I did enjoy the show's humor and the thought experiment of how people respond to something miraculous when no further information is forthcoming.
While it might not be the strongest script for Trap Door Theatre's repertoire, The Man Who Fell with the Rain stays true to the company's commitment to avant-garde storytelling.
